title: AI-Generated Code Detector
blurb: Reads the stylistic tells of AI-written code — and is honest that none of them are proof.

steps.say: There is no reliable detector for AI-written code. What there are, are stylistic tells — and this tool surfaces them honestly, without ever claiming a verdict. Let's start with a snippet in the unmistakable AI house style.

A docstring on every function, a comment before every single step, defensive try-except wrapping, tidy uniform naming throughout. A human can write like this — but models do it relentlessly, and that relentlessness is the signal.
Analyze. The stylistic pass runs entirely in your browser — no model needed for that part — and, if a server key is set, an independent LLM is asked for its own opinion alongside.

The headline is worded carefully: it counts AI-style signals, and says in the same breath that it is not a verdict. That restraint is the point — the number of signals is a prompt to look closer, not a label.

Below, the specific patterns it matched, each with why it is associated with generated code — and beside them, the independent LLM's leaning and confidence, kept separate so you can see where the two agree or disagree.

And the limits, stated without hedging: every signal here is individually weak and trivially fakeable in either direction. A careful human writes clean, documented code; any model can be told to write messy code. Treat this as a lens, never a ruling.
